cases.purpose: INFORM originates on UDP 68, receives the matching ACK on UDP 68, and prints its fields.
cases.oracle: RFC 2131 s2 and s4.3 field layout and RFC 2132 option encodings, checked by an independent Python decoder over sniffed frames; no GNU reference tool exists for this builtin.
cases.comparison: The private peer records both datagrams; check the client source and ACK destination ports and the decoded output.

files.case.sh:
IP=/usr/bin/ip
PY=/usr/bin/python3
H=/opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/mig-w2-dhcp4.py
die() { echo "SETUP-FAILED $*"; exit 90; }
/usr/bin/mount -t sysfs sysfs /sys || die sysfs
$IP link set lo up || die lo
$IP link add veth0 address 02:00:00:00:0a:01 type veth peer name veth1 address 02:00:00:00:0a:02 || die veth
echo 0 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/all/rp_filter || die rpf-all
echo 0 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/veth0/rp_filter || die rpf-veth0
exec 7<>sync.fifo
"$PY" "$H" peer full sync.fifo 2> peer.err &
peer=$!
read -t 20 -u 7 line || die peer-pid
[[ $line == "pid=$peer" ]] || die "peer-pid-$line"
$IP link set veth1 netns "$peer" || die move
read -t 20 -u 7 line || die peer-ready
[[ $line == ready ]] || die "peer-$line"
$IP addr add 192.0.2.10/24 dev veth0 || die addr
$IP link set veth0 up || die up
settle() { read -t "$1" -u 7 line; }
bashdhcp inform -i veth0 -a 192.0.2.10 -t 1000 > out.txt 2> err.txt; rc=$?
echo "inform-rc=$rc"
echo "$(< out.txt)"
echo "stderr=[$(< err.txt)]"
settle 0.3
kill "$peer"; wait "$peer" 2>/dev/null

"$PY" - <<'PYCODE'
import json, os
with open(os.path.join(os.environ.get('HOME', '/tmp/parity-home'), 'w2-peer.json')) as f:
    log = json.load(f)
incoming = [e for e in log if e['dir'] == 'in']
outgoing = [e for e in log if e['dir'] == 'out']
print('client-port=' + str(incoming[0]['sport']) if len(incoming) == 1 else 'client-packet-count=' + str(len(incoming)))
print('ack-port=' + str(outgoing[0]['to'][1]) if len(outgoing) == 1 else 'ack-packet-count=' + str(len(outgoing)))
PYCODE
